problem: Existing semantic/language-conditioned safety methods (HJ reachability, CBF, planners) need a user to supply safety rules that reference precise semantics of a known environment. Robots therefore cannot reason about contextual safety (wet-floor signs, cone lines, pedestrians, sidewalks vs grass) in unseen open-world settings.
motivation: Safe behavior in open-world deployment depends on context that cannot be specified a priori, so the robot must infer safety rules online from what it sees. VLMs can reason about context, but their outputs are noisy and non-spatial, so they must be grounded into metric safe sets and enforced with formal guarantees that account for perception errors.
key_idea: Use a VLM to infer context-dependent safety predicates (spatial operator + semantic class) from images online, ground them via open-vocabulary segmentation and depth into a signed-distance barrier function, and enforce it with a CBF-QP that carries probabilistic guarantees under perception failure.
insight: Structured VLM output (predicate operators, safety logic, chain-of-thought) is what makes contextual reasoning reliable: removing CoT drops safe-region prediction from 91% to 61%, and removing safety logic lowers unsafe-region prediction from 85% to 80%. Reasoning online is essential: a No-Context baseline with pre-generated rules prevents only 16.6% of unsafe tasks versus 93.3% for CORE. A bigger or slower VLM is not better (Qwen3-VL 30B with reasoning is 26.6s and worse than Gemma 3 27B).
method: Structured safety representation: the VLM outputs predicates pairing a spatial operator (ON, NEAR, AROUND, BETWEEN) with a semantic class, split into safe and unsafe sets, plus chain-of-thought justification, in JSON; the safety logic is given in the system prompt.
Contextual reasoning: 4-bit Gemma 3 27B identifies hazard indicators, social zones, semantic barriers and navigable surfaces, then picks operators per context.
Image-space safe set: SAM3 open-vocabulary segmentation; ON/NEAR take the class pixels, AROUND dilates the mask (50 px kernel), BETWEEN takes the convex hull; safe = union(safe) minus union(unsafe).

Barrier construction: project pixels to 3D with depth, accumulate safe/unsafe counts in a 2D grid (0.2 m), threshold P(safe) at 0.5, and define h(x) as a signed distance field over the safe set with an analytic gradient from grid lookup.
CBF enforcement: QP min ||u-u_nom||^2 s.t. <grad h, f+gu> >= -alpha(h), alpha(x)=0.25x, solved with CVXPY; it is planner-agnostic and always feasible.

Perception-uncertainty guarantee: a detection probability function m(.) and an inverse regularized distance d^-1(r)=c/(r+l), analyzed with nonnegative supermartingales and Ville's inequality, gives P[exists t: x_t not in S] <= delta given k* observations per traversal; a union bound with gamma covers worst-case contexts.
Real-world depth handling: Spot's depth is noisy, so DepthAnythingV3 is used with median-fit scale alignment; measurements within 3 m or beyond 7 m are discarded.

setting.backbone: Gemma 3 27B VLM (4-bit, frozen) + SAM3 segmentation + CBF-QP controller
setting.training_data: none (training-free; pretrained VLM and SAM3 used off the shelf)
setting.action_space: continuous velocity (2D linear velocity + yaw rate) filtered by a CBF-QP, nominal controller is waypoint follower + PID
setting.simulator: NVIDIA Isaac Sim (warehouse, hospital, outdoor residential) + real Boston Dynamics Spot
setting.privileged: none (the Oracle baseline receives ground-truth constraints, but CORE does not)

numbers.extra: 3 environments x 4 tasks (2 safe, 2 unsafe) x 5 repeats = 60 evaluations; the paper's own task set, not an official split

numbers_note: Not a standard navigation benchmark; the numbers come from the paper's own safety task suites. The safe-traversal guarantee is delta=0.1 (a 90% certificate), reported in text.
results: In simulation CORE reaches 95.0% total success (96.6% safe, 93.3% unsafe), close to the Oracle with ground-truth rules (98.3%), and beats No Context (55.0%; 16.6% unsafe prevented) and Geometric (50.0%; 0% unsafe prevented). On the Spot robot CORE gets 86.6% versus 50.0% for the Geometric baseline. A certificate at delta=0.1 is obtained and empirically consistent with about 93% unsafe-task success.
limitations: Uncertainty model uses an average VLM error rate, not per-frame uncertainty; VLM latency (~4 s) and missed detections at key timesteps cause failures.
Grounding errors (depth noise creating ghost obstacles, misdetected semantics) drive the higher real-world failure rate; measurements within 3 m or beyond 7 m are discarded.
Restricted to control-affine systems, static spatial safe sets (no temporal logic), and the theory assumes safe initialization; small evaluation (60 sim / 30 real trials).
